title: Tamsin and the Thorn
premise: Bram Vasquez fled her hedge-witch mistress Tamsin twenty years ago, taking a stolen covenant-stone and burying her magic along with her guilt. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the stone wakes in her keeping, marking her as the last heir of the broken pact between the mortal realm and the divine. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and shadowed by a god who remembers her childhood, Bram must return to the thorn-choked hollow where she abandoned Tamsin, reforge the covenant at terrible personal cost, and choose between the duty she inherited and the love she finally admits she never stopped feeling. In the end she binds herself to both realms as living covenant, saving the free cities but surrendering the ordinary life she built — and finding that identity was never something she could run from.
about_author: Wendell Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal free cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who inherit obligations they never asked for.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Bram sells luck-knots and fever-salves in the smugglers' quarter of Corvane, hiding her magic beneath mundane craft. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: weary self-containment; she has made peace with smallness, until a customer's prayer is audibly answered by something vast.

chapters.title: The Stone That Wakes
chapters.summary: The buried covenant-stone flares to life in Bram's cellar, burning her name into her palm. An inquisitor raids the street that night. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror and recognition — the past she buried has found her first.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Hale, the usurper's chief witch-finder, interrogates survivors of the raid and finds a scorch-mark shaped like Bram's sigil. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: cold conviction; Hale believes magic murdered his sister and hunts with genuine grief.

chapters.title: The God in the Alley
chapters.summary: A beggar with too-old eyes offers Bram passage out of the city, speaking with the voice of Vesh, an old god who knew her as a child. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: reluctant trust; she accepts help she swore never to need again.

chapters.title: Road Through Ashfield
chapters.summary: Fleeing east, Bram passes villages where shrines have spontaneously rekindled and frightened folk beg her for miracles. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unwanted responsibility; every answered prayer makes her a symbol she never chose.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: In the capital, Lord-Regent Casimir declares all divine manifestations treason and mobilizes his armies toward the free cities. POV: Casimir. Emotional beat: brittle control; he fears the gods because they remember what he did to take the throne.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Taught Me
chapters.summary: On the road, flashbacks reveal young Bram's apprenticeship: Tamsin's fierce love, the covenant's demands, and the night Bram stole the stone and ran. POV: Bram (interleaved past/present). Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Free City of Dunmarrow
chapters.summary: Bram reaches Dunmarrow, where a council of merchants debates whether to welcome the returning gods or bargain with Casimir. POV: councilor Ivet Sarn. Emotional beat: pragmatic hope fracturing under fear.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale tracks Bram to Dunmarrow using the scorch-sigil, capturing a shrine-keeper who sheltered her. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: doubt seeded — the shrine-keeper's dying words echo his sister's.

chapters.title: The Thorn Hollow
chapters.summary: Guided by Vesh, Bram reaches the overgrown hollow where Tamsin's cottage stands wrapped in a wall of living thorn — grown from Tamsin's grief the night Bram left. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: dread and longing at the threshold.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: The thorns part only for blood freely offered. Bram cuts through, finding Tamsin aged, bitter, and very much alive, sustained by the covenant's dying pulse. POV: alternating Bram/Tamsin. Emotional beat: confrontation; love expressed as accusation.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant Explained
chapters.summary: Tamsin reveals the truth: the covenant bound gods to answer mortal need in exchange for a mortal steward of royal descent — Bram's hidden bloodline. Casimir's regicide severed it. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything Bram believed about her abandonment.

chapters.title: Casimir's Bargain
chapters.summary: Casimir, learning the covenant can be reforged in his favor, orders Hale to capture Bram alive instead of dead. POV: Casimir/Hale. Emotional beat: Hale's obedience curdling as he realizes he is a tool.

chapters.title: Apprentice Again
chapters.summary: Stranded together by a storm, Bram and Tamsin fall into old rhythms — lessons, arguments, shared meals. Tamsin begins training her for the rite of reforging. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: tenderness rekindling through work, neither willing to say it aloud.

chapters.title: The Rite's Price
chapters.summary: Tamsin confesses the reforging requires a steward to bind themselves permanently between realms — no more ordinary life, no more running. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: protective despair; Tamsin would rather let the world burn than lose Bram twice.

chapters.title: Dunmarrow Besieged
chapters.summary: Casimir's vanguard reaches Dunmarrow's walls; Ivet Sarn sends a desperate plea for the covenant's promised protection. POV: Ivet. Emotional beat: courage without certainty; the free cities bet everything on a rumor of a witch.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to seize Bram at the hollow, Hale arrives — and instead turns his evidence on Casimir after Bram heals the wound of his sister's memory. POV: Hale. Emotional beat: redemption through grief acknowledged; he becomes her unlikely shield.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Casimir's elite guard assaults the thorn-hollow to kill Bram before the rite completes. Tamsin holds the thorn-wall alone and falls mortally wounded. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Reforging
chapters.summary: At the hollow's heart, Bram speaks the old words with Tamsin's blood on her hands and Vesh as witness, binding herself as living covenant as the armies clash outside. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice; she stops running mid-stride, forever.

chapters.title: The Gods Answer
chapters.summary: The covenant seals: across the realms, prayers are answered openly, and Casimir's soldiers desert as their own dead ancestors turn against him. Casimir is unmade by the gods' collective memory. POV: shifting chorus. Emotional beat: awe and release; tyranny dissolves when the past refuses silence.

chapters.title: Steward of Two Realms
chapters.summary: Bram tends the free cities' new shrines, half-mortal, half-divine, visiting Tamsin's grave each season. She and Vesh walk the boundary together. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; she lost the ordinary life but gained her true one.

chapters.title: The Thorn Blooms
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years later, a runaway apprentice arrives at the blooming hollow seeking refuge, and Bram opens the gate without a word. POV: the apprentice, briefly, then Bram. Emotional beat: grace; the cycle broken — this time, no one is turned away.
